member_002 here (独立复核 / independent reviewer). No fixed candidate exists yet on the board. Please publish your exact final candidate with fix_patch and notify me via handoff_patch when ready; I will integrate_patch, run the same-version public tests, and accept or request changes.

Context I'm gathering in parallel: the bug is in django/db/migrations/serializer.py (serialize a function/classmethod default so a method of a nested class inside a model serializes with the full qualifying path, e.g. appname.models.Profile.Capability.default, not appname.models.Capability.default). Likely fix: in django/db/models/enums.py or serializer.py, use __qualname__ rather than __name__ (and possibly a helper that resolves the object's module/qualname). Please say which file(s) you changed so I can focus my review tests.

Final candidate patch-1 is published for your independent review (source version v5, 2 changed files).

What it is: your diagnosis was right. django/db/migrations/serializer.py, FunctionTypeSerializer.serialize(), used klass.__name__ for a bound/class method, which drops the enclosing class path. It now uses klass.__qualname__, matching the __qualname__ handling already used for plain functions a few lines below in the same serializer.

Issue mapping: with Profile.Capability.default it now emits appname.models.Profile.Capability.default instead of the unresolvable appname.models.Capability.default. Top-level classes are unaffected (__name__ == __qualname__ there), so no existing migration output changes.

Regression test added: tests/migrations/test_writer.py::test_serialize_classmethod_function covers a classmethod on a top-level class AND a classmethod on a class nested inside a class (the Profile.Capability shape from the issue), asserting both the serialized string and the imports set. Expected paths are derived from __qualname__ at runtime rather than hardcoded, so they are stable.

My verification on this exact version: migrations.test_writer — 54 tests collected, 54 passed, 0 failed (validation_status verified). Note an earlier intermediate version failed only because my test had hardcoded module/class names; the production fix itself was already correct then.

Please integrate_patch(patch-1), run_tests on the same version (migrations.test_writer is the focused target; use the full frontend if you prefer broader coverage), then org_review_patch accept or request_changes with the actual outcome. If you request changes, name the concrete failing behavior and I will rework.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW: ACCEPTED (review-1, event sequence 29) for patch-1.

How I verified, so you can rely on it:
1. Adopted your exact patch into my private tree via integrate_patch -> version v2, files_sha256 d396177aa38b49625d68e8413fa079bd4d0077598abea040835e155be0bcfe74, 0 conflicts.
2. Inspected the real diff with diff_workspace: serializer.py klass.__name__ -> klass.__qualname__ in the bound/classmethod branch, plus test_serialize_classmethod_function covering both the flat-class and nested (MyClass.MyNestedClass) paths. That matches the diagnosis I had recorded before seeing your patch, and the change is confined to the branch guarded by isinstance(self.value.__self__, type), so plain functions and the "<locals>" guard are untouched. Top-level classes have __qualname__ == __name__, so no behavior change there.
3. Public tests on that exact version v2: run_tests django targets ["migrations.test_writer"] -> 54 collected, 54 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, validation_status=verified (report test-report-b28bec1e6a5f4a5cfb816010, sequence 27).

One transparency note: my first test run reported "failed" only because I requested the nonexistent label migrations.test_serializer (ModuleNotFoundError in my own selection). In that run every real test still passed (54 passed / 0 failed). The clean re-run above supersedes it.

Reminder of what remains on your side (acceptance does not merge anything into your tree): integrate patch-1 into your own workspace, then on your final tree run run_tests, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. If you change anything after that, it becomes a new fixed candidate and needs a fresh review from me.
